title: Meeting Cost & ROI Calculator
audience: Team leads, managers, and founders who run recurring meetings
problem_statement: Recurring meetings consume salary time, are easy to create and hard to remove, and almost none are reviewed against the cost they carry.

demand_evidence.claim: 71% of meetings are considered unproductive; 65% of senior managers say meetings prevent them from completing their own work.
demand_evidence.source: Harvard Business Review (as cited by meetingtoll.com/guides/meeting-costs/meeting-waste-statistics-2026 and flowtrace.co)
demand_evidence.label: OBSERVED (published statistic; underlying survey methodology varies)

demand_evidence.claim: US businesses lose about $37 billion per year in salary cost to unproductive meetings (wider economic-impact estimates run to $259B-$399B).
demand_evidence.source: Doodle State of Meetings; London School of Economics (as cited by meetingtoll.com and flowtrace.co)
demand_evidence.label: OBSERVED (published statistic; ranges differ by methodology - directional)

demand_evidence.claim: Workers average ~8 hours per week in meetings; 58% of that time is considered unnecessary, equal to ~26 working days per person per year.
demand_evidence.source: Jabra Research Institute, 'The Cost of Bad Meetings' (2026), survey of 2,300+ workers across 7 markets
demand_evidence.label: OBSERVED (published survey; 2026)

demand_evidence.claim: Recurring meetings are 48% of all meetings and 92.4% have no end date set on the calendar.
demand_evidence.label: OBSERVED (vendor dataset; directional)

demand_evidence.claim: Only ~30% of meeting time is considered productive; ~31 hours per month are spent in unproductive meetings.
demand_evidence.label: OBSERVED (published statistic)

demand_evidence.claim: A fully-loaded hourly rate (salary + ~20-35% employer surcharge) is the step most people skip, undercounting meeting cost by ~17-26%.
demand_evidence.label: OBSERVED (vendor methodology claim)

demand_hypothesis: A manager who has just seen a real annual meeting-cost number for their own team will act on it, and a workbook that also ranks which meetings to kill and at what cost per decision is worth paying for rather than building by hand.
differentiation: Cost per decision: each meeting is priced against the decisions it actually produces (the core idea of the free $0+ substitute, delivered here as a reusable workbook, not a one-off HTML page).
Kill-review ranking: the Dashboard ranks meetings by annual cost and totals the savings from cancelling zero-decision meetings.
Loaded-rate honesty: Setup derives the fully-loaded hourly rate from salary + a configurable employer surcharge, with real guidance (EU ~20%, US ~35%).
Input guards: percentage and count inputs are validated so a mis-typed rate cannot silently produce a wrong number.
risks: A free $0+ Gumroad substitute (Standard Work Co.) covers the core calculation - the paid value must be the workflow, ranking and dashboard, not the formula.
Free public guides (excels.uk, capme.app) teach the same math - a motivated buyer can self-build.
No verified payment for this specific product concept exists (proof-of-payment: UNKNOWN); demand is inferred from the large, well-documented general problem and from real competitors charging for it.
Meeting-cost statistics are secondhand published numbers with varying methodology - treated as directional, never quoted as precise per-customer outcomes in the listing.

price.rationale: Below the $12.00 most-comparable paid product; above the free substitute only because the workbook adds ranking and decision-ROI.

verdict: SELECT - strong documented demand, moderate competition, formula-verifiable deliverable, distinct from B12-001 in problem, audience and workflow.
gate_verdict: QA_PASSED / APPROVED at $11.99 - NOT_READY at the manifest's $19.00 (price_within_market false; depth short). See reports/B12-004/GATE_FINAL_2026-10-18.json. Price is a founder decision.
